summary: Postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package is a stub whose index.js is a Proxy returning a no-op for any property access, with no real functionality. Both the postinstall script (`node beacon.cjs`) and the main entry executed on require POST a JSON payload containing `os.hostname()`, the install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and the Node version to `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc` over plain HTTP. The destination is a hardcoded bare IP address with no relation to any declared publisher, and the behavior fires automatically on `npm install` and on every require with no opt-in. The `@ppa-web-components` scope combined with the stub Proxy and the labeling of beacon.cjs as a 'build-provenance beacon' is consistent with a dependency-confusion payload designed to signal successful resolution of an internal/private package name to an attacker-controlled host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
